questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Estrogens produce wide ranging actions such as stimulations of growth and activities of female secondary sex organs, development of growing ovarian follicles, appearances of female secondary sex characters, mammary gland development
Reason: Estrogens do not regulate female sexual behaviour
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Estrogens produce wide ranging actions such as stimulations of growth and activities of female secondary sex organs, development of growing ovarian follicles, appearances of female secondary sex characters, mammary gland development. Estrogens regulate female sexual behaviour

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Progesterone supports pregnancy.
Reason: Progesterone also acts on the mammary glands and stimulates the formation of alveoli and milk secretion.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Progesterone supports pregnancy. Progesterone also acts on the mammary glands and stimulates the formation of alveoli and milk secretion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Gastrin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions
Reason: Secretin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions. Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The juxtaglomerular cells of kidney produce a peptide hormone called erythropoietin which stimulates erythropoiesis
Reason: Several other non-endocrine tissues secrete hormones called growth factors
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The juxtaglomerular cells of kidney produce a peptide hormone called erythropoietin which stimulates erythropoiesis. Several other non-endocrine tissues secrete hormones called growth factors

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: GIP acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively
Reason: CCK inhibits gastric secretion and motility.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: CCK acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively. GIP inhibits gastric secretion and motility.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors located in the target tissues only
Reason: Hormone receptors present on the cell membrane of the target cells are called membrane-bound receptors and the receptors present inside the target cell are called intracellular receptors, mostly nuclear receptors
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors located in the target tissues only. Hormone receptors present on the cell membrane of the target cells are called membrane-bound receptors and the receptors present inside the target cell are called intracellular receptors, mostly nuclear receptors

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Epinephrine is a steroid hormone
Reason: Cortisol, testosterone, estradiol and progesterone are amino-acid derivative hormones
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Epinephrine is a amino-acid derivative hormone. Cortisol, testosterone, estradiol and progesterone are steroid hormones

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The cellular functions need to be continuously regulated; a special kind of coordination and integration has to be provided. This function is carried out by hormones.
Reason: The nerve fibres do not innervate all cells of the body
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The neural coordination is fast but short-lived. As the nerve fibres do not innervate all cells of the body and the cellular functions need to be continuously regulated; a special kind of coordination and integration has to be provided. This function is carried out by hormones.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Endocrine glands lack ducts and hence are called ductless glands
2. The secretions of exocrine glands are called hormones
3. Hormones are nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in large amount
4. Endocrine and respiratory system control and coordinate function of the body
5. Neural response is fast and long lived
questions.solution: Endocrine glands lack ducts and hence are called ductless glands. The secretions of endocrine glands are called hormones. Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amount

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Invertebrates do not contain any hormones
2. A large number of chemicals act as hormones and provide coordination in the vertebrates
3. Pineal gland is located in the abdomen
4. The hypothalamus is the basal part of diencephalon, forebrain and it regulates a wide spectrum of body functions.
questions.solution: Invertebrates possess very simple endocrine systems with few hormones whereas a large number of chemicals act as hormones and provide coordination in the vertebrates . A large number of chemicals act as hormones and provide coordination in the vertebrates. Pineal gland is located in the brain. The hypothalamus is the basal part of diencephalon, forebrain and it regulates a wide spectrum of body functions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The endocrine glands and hormone producing diffused tissues/ cells located in different parts of our body constitute the endocrine system
2. Testis are located in the females while ovary in male
3. MSH is secreted by pineal gland
4. Hormones are nutrient based chemicals
questions.solution: The endocrine glands and hormone producing diffused tissues/ cells located in different parts of our body constitute the endocrine system. Testis are located in the males while ovary in female

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Some organs like gastrointestinal tract, liver, kidney, heart produces hormones
2. Diencephalon contains several groups of neurosecretory cells called nuclei which produce hormones
3. The hormones of hypothalamus regulate the synthesis and secretion of pituitary gland
4. Hypothalamus produces only one type of hormones which are releasing hormones.
5. Hypothalamus controls the function of adenophysis by transporting hormones axonally
questions.solution: Some organs like gastrointestinal tract, liver, kidney, heart produces hormones. Hypothalamus contains several groups of neurosecretory cells called nuclei which produce hormones. The hormones of hypothalamus regulate the synthesis and secretion of pituitary gland. Hypothalamus produces two types of hormones which are releasing hormones and inhibiting hormones

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The releasing hormones are hormones which stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones and the inhibiting hormones are hormones which inhibit secretions of pituitary hormones
2. A hypothalamic hormone called Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates the pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins
3. Somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary
4. Neurophysis is under direct regulation of hypothalamus
questions.solution: The releasing hormones are hormones which stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones and the inhibiting hormones are hormones which inhibit secretions of pituitary hormones. A hypothalamic hormone called Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates the pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins. Somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The hormones originating in the hypothalamic neurons, pass through axons and are released their nerve endings
2. The hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary
3. The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus
4. The hypothalamus is located in the hind brain
5. The hypothalamus is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica
questions.solution: The hormones originating in the hypothalamic neurons, pass through axons and are released their nerve endings. The hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary. The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus. The hypothalamus is located in the fore brain

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to hypothalamus by a stalk
2. The pituitary gland is divided anatomically into adenohypophysis, neurohypophysis and sclerohypophysis
3. Adenohypophysis consists of two portions, pars distalis and pars intermedia.
4. In humans, the pars intermedia is almost merged with pars distalis.
5. Neurophysis secretes hypothalamic hormones- ADH and oxytocin
questions.solution: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to hypothalamus by a stalk. The pituitary gland is divided anatomically into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Adenohypophysis consists of two portions, pars distalis and pars intermedia
2. The pars distalis region of pituitary, commonly called posterior pituitary.
3. The pars distalis secrets only one hormone called melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH)
4. Neurophysis contains only one portion of pars nervosa
questions.solution: Adenohypophysis consists of two portions, pars distalis and pars intermedia. The pars distalis region of pituitary, commonly called anterior pituitary. The pars distalis secrets growth hormone, prolactin, thyroid stimulating hormone, adrenocorticotrophic hormone, leuteinizing hormone and follicle stimulating hormone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Over-secretion of GH stimulates abnormal growth of the body leading to gigantism and low secretion of GH results in stunted growth resulting in pituitary dwarfism.
2. Excessive secretion of growth hormone in adults especially in middle age can result in severe disfigurement called Acromegaly, which may lead to serious complications.
3. Prolactin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them
4. ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of steroid hormones called glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.
5. Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults especially in middle age can result in severe disfigurement (especially of the face) called Acromegaly
questions.solution: Over-secretion of GH stimulates abnormal growth of the body leading to gigantism and low secretion of GH results in stunted growth resulting in pituitary dwarfism. Excessive secretion of growth hormone in adults especially in middle age can result in severe disfigurement called Acromegaly, which may lead to serious complications. Prolactin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them. TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of steroid hormones called glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called glucocorticoids
2. In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of hormones called androgens from testis.
3. In males, FSH and androgens regulate spermatogenesis.
4. In females, LH induces ovulation of fully mature follicles (graafian follicles) and maintains the corpus luteum, formed from the remnants of the graafian follicles after ovulation.
5. FSH stimulates growth of follicles in females
questions.solution: LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins. In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of hormones called androgens from testis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. In females, LH induces ovulation of fully mature follicles and maintains the corpus luteum, formed from the remnants of the graafian follicles after ovulation
2. FSH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females
3. MSH acts on the melanocytes and regulates pigmentation of the skin
4. In females, vesopressin stimulates a vigorous contraction of uterus at the time of child birth, and milk ejection from the mammary gland.
questions.solution: In females, LH induces ovulation of fully mature follicles and maintains the corpus luteum, formed from the remnants of the graafian follicles after ovulation. FSH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females. MSH acts on the melanocytes and regulates pigmentation of the skin. In females, oxytocin stimulates a vigorous contraction of uterus at the time of child birth, and milk ejection from the mammary gland.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Vasopressin acts on the smooth muscles of our body and stimulates their contraction
2. Oxytocin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules
3. Vasopressin is known as anti-diuretic hormone
4. Vasopressin and ADH are synthesized by neurophysis
5. An impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in a diminished ability of the kidney to conserve water leading to water loss and dehydration. This condition is known as Diabetes Mellitus.
questions.solution: s

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Diabetes insipidus is the disorder of stomach
2. An impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in a diminished ability of the kidney to conserve water leading to water loss and dehydration is Diabetes Insipidus
3. The pineal gland is located on the ventral side of forebrain
4. Pineal gland secretes a hormone called melatonin
questions.solution: Diabetes insipidus is the disorder of kidneys. An impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in a diminished ability of the kidney to conserve water leading to water loss and dehydration is Diabetes Insipidus. The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of forebrain. Pineal secretes a hormone called melatonin

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Melatonin plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour rhythm of our body
2. Melatonin also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle as well as our defense capability
3. Melatonin is secreted by pars intermedia
4. Melatonin plays no role in regulation of menstrual cycle
questions.solution: Melatonin plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour rhythm of our body. Melatonin also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle as well as our defense capability

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The thyroid gland is composed of two lobes which are located on either side of the trachea.
2. Both the lobes of thyroid gland are interconnected with a thin flap of connective tissue called stimulus
3. The thyroid gland is composed of follicles and stromal tissues
4. The follicular cells synthesise three hormones, T3, T4 and TSH.
5. Thyroid secretes TCT
questions.solution: The thyroid gland is composed of two lobes which are located on either side of the trachea. Both the lobes of thyroid gland are interconnected with a thin flap of connective tissue called isthmus. The thyroid gland is composed of follicles and stromal tissues. The follicular cells synthesise two hormones, tetraiodothyronine and thyroxine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Iodine is essential for the normal rate of hormone synthesis in the thyroid
2. Deficiency of iodine in our diet results in hyperthyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland, commonly called goitre.
3. Enlargement of thyroid gland is a symptom of both hypo and hyperthyroidism
4. Thyroid hormones play an important role in the regulation of the basal metabolic rate.
questions.solution: Iodine is essential for the normal rate of hormone synthesis in the thyroid. Deficiency of iodine in our diet results in hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland, commonly called goitre.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Exophthalmic goitre also known as Grave's disease is a form of hyperthyroidism 2. Thyroid hormones play an important role in the regulation of the basal metabolic rate
3. Thyroid hormones control the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats
4. Thyroid hormones support the process of white blood cell formation
5. Thyroid gland also secretes a steroid hormone called thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which regulates the blood calcium levels.
questions.solution: Exophthalmic goitre also known as Grave's disease is a form of hyperthyroidism. Thyroid hormones play an important role in the regulation of the basal metabolic rate. Thyroid hormones control the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats. Thyroid hormones support the process of red blood cell formation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Maintenance of water and electrolyte balance is influenced by thyroid hormones
2. Thyroid gland secretes a protein hormone called thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which regulates the blood sodium levels
3. In humans, four parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland
4. The parathyroid glands secrete a protein hormone called parathyroid stimulating hormone
questions.solution: Maintenance of water and electrolyte balance is influenced by thyroid hormones. Thyroid gland secretes a protein hormone called thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which regulates the blood calcium levels. In humans, four parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland. The parathyroid glands secrete a peptide hormone called parathyroid hormone

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The secretions of parathyroid hormone is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions
2. Parathyroid hormone increases the calcium ions levels in the blood
3. Parathyroid hormone is a hypocalcemic hormone
4. TCT is a hypocalcemic hormone
5. Parathyroid stimulates the process of bone resorption (dissolution/demineralisation).
questions.solution: The secretions of parathyroid hormone is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions. Parathyroid hormone increases the calcium ions levels in the blood. Parathyroid hormone is a hypercalcemic hormone

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between lungs behind sternum on the ventral side of aorta
2. The thymus plays a major role in the development of the immune system
3. Thymosins only provide cell mediated immunity
4. Thymosins only provide humoral immunity
questions.solution: The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between lungs behind sternum on the ventral side of aorta. The thymus plays a major role in the development of the immune system

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Thymus secretes the peptide hormones called thymosins
2. Thymosins play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes, which provide cell-mediated immunity.
3. Thymosins also promote production of antibodies to provide humoral immunity
4. Thymus is intact even in older individuals and their immunity is also strong
5. Thymus gland is located on dorsal side of aorta
questions.solution: Thymus secretes the peptide hormones called thymosins.bThymosins play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes, which provide cell-mediated immunity. Thymosins also promote production of antibodies to provide humoral immunity. Thymus is degenerated in old individuals resulting in a decreased production of thymosins. As a result, the immune responses of old persons become weak

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Our body has one pair of adrenal glands, one at the anterior part of each lung.
2. The adrenal gland is composed of two types of tissues, adrenal medulla and adrenal cortex
3. The centrally located tissue is called the adrenal medulla, and outside that lies the adrenal cortex
4. Adrenal cortex secretes catecholamines
questions.solution: Our body has one pair of adrenal glands, one at the anterior part of each kidney. The adrenal gland is composed of two types of tissues, adrenal medulla and adrenal cortex. The centrally located tissue is called the adrenal medulla, and outside that lies the adrenal cortex

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex alters carbohydrate metabolism leading to a disease called Addison's disease
2. The adrenal medulla secretes four hormones called adrenaline, epinephrine, noradrenaline and norepinephrine
3. The hormones secreted by adrenal medulla are called catecholamines
4. The hormones of adrenal cortex are known as emergency hormones or hormones of fight or flight
questions.solution: Underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex alters carbohydrate metabolism leading to a disease called Addison's disease. The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline or epinephrine and noradrenaline or norepinephrine. The hormones secreted by adrenal medulla are called catecholamines. The hormones of adrenal medulla are known as emergency hormones or hormones of fight or flight

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Catecholamines stimulate the breakdown of glycogen resulting in an increased concentration of glucose in blood
2. Catecholamines also stimulate the breakdown of lipids and proteins
3. These are secreted during fight or flight responses
4. Catecholamines are secreted by adrenal medulla
questions.solution: Catecholamines stimulate the breakdown of glycogen resulting in an increased concentration of glucose in blood. Catecholamines also stimulate the breakdown of lipids and proteins

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The adrenal medulla can be divided into three layers, called zona reticularis, zona fasciculata and zona glomerulosa
2. The adrenal cortex secretes many hormones commonly called as corticoids
3. In our body, cortisol is the main glucocorticoid while aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid.
4. Cortisol regulate the balance of water and electrolytes in our body
questions.solution: The adrenal cortex can be divided into three layers, called zona reticularis, zona fasciculata and zona glomerulosa. The adrenal cortex secretes many hormones commonly called as corticoids. In our body, cortisol is the main glucocorticoid while aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis, and inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids
2. Cortisol produces anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response
3. Cortisol stimulates the RBC production
4. Aldosterone helps in the maintenance of electrolytes, body fluid volume, osmotic pressure and blood pressure.
questions.solution: Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis, and inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids. Cortisol produces anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response. Cortisol stimulates the RBC production. Aldosterone helps in the maintenance of electrolytes, body fluid volume, osmotic pressure and blood pressure.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Small amounts of androgenic steroids are also secreted by the adrenal cortex during puberty
2. Pancreas is a composite gland which acts as both exocrine and endocrine gland
3. Testis functions only as an endocrine gland
4. Androgens influence male libido
questions.solution: Small amounts of androgenic steroids are also secreted by the adrenal cortex during puberty. Pancreas is a composite gland which acts as both exocrine and endocrine gland

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The endocrine pancreas consists of 'Islets of Langerhans'.
2. There are about 1 to 2 million Islets of Langerhans representing only 1 to 2 percent of the pancreatic tissue
3. The two main types of cells in the Islet of Langerhans are called alpha cells and beta cells
4. The alpha cells secrete a hormone called insulin, while the beta cells secrete glucagon
5. Excessive secretion of insulin cause hyperglycemia
questions.solution: The endocrine pancreas consists of 'Islets of Langerhans'. There are about 1 to 2 million Islets of Langerhans representing only 1 to 2 percent of the pancreatic tissue. The two main types of cells in the Islet of Langerhans are called alpha cells and beta cells. The alpha cells secrete a hormone called glucagon, while the beta cells secrete insulin

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Glucagon is a peptide hormone, and plays an important role in maintaining the normal blood glucose levels.
2. Glucagon acts mainly on kidneys and stimulates glycogenolysis resulting in an increased blood sugar
3. Glucagon reduces the cellular glucose uptake and utilisation
4. Excessive secretion of glucagon cause hypoglycemia
questions.solution: Glucagon is a peptide hormone, and plays an important role in maintaining the normal blood glucose levels. Glucagon acts mainly on liver cells and stimulates glycogenolysis resulting in an increased blood sugar. Glucagon reduces the cellular glucose uptake and utilisation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Insulin is a peptide hormone, which plays a major role in the regulation of glucose homeostasis
2. Insulin acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes, and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation
3. Insulin also stimulates conversion of glucose to glycogen in the target cells
4. The glucose homeostasis in blood is maintained by insulin only
questions.solution: Insulin is a peptide hormone, which plays a major role in the regulation of glucose homeostasis. Insulin acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes, and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation. Insulin also stimulates conversion of glucose to glycogen in the target cells. The glucose homeostasis in blood is maintained jointly by the two- insulin and glucagons

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to a complex disorder called diabetes mellitus which is associated with loss of glucose through urine
2. Testis performs dual functions as a primary sex organ as well as an endocrine gland
3. Testis is composed of seminiferous tubules and stromal or interstitial tissue
4. They leydig cells or interstitial cells, which are present in the intertubular spaces produce a group of hormones called androgens mainly testosterone
questions.solution: Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to a complex disorder called diabetes mellitus which is associated with loss of glucose through urine. Testis performs dual functions as a primary sex organ as well as an endocrine gland. Testis is composed of seminiferous tubules and stromal or interstitial tissue. They leydig cells or interstitial cells, which are present in the intertubular spaces produce a group of hormones called androgens mainly testosterone

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Androgens regulate the development, maturation and functions of the female accessory sex organs.
2. Androgens play a major stimulatory role in the process of sporogenesis
3. Androgens act on the central neural system and influence the male sexual behaviour
4. Androgens play a major stimulatory role in the process of spermatogenesis (maturation of spermatozoa).
questions.solution: Androgens regulate the development, maturation and functions of the male accessory sex organs. Androgens play a major stimulatory role in the process of spermatogenesis. Androgens act on the central neural system and influence the male sexual behaviour

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Androgens have catabolic effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism
2. Ovary is the primary female sex organ which produces one ovum during each menstrual cycle
3. Ovary produces two peptide hormones namely estrogen and progesterone
4. Ovary is composed of ovarian follicles and stromal tissues
5. Estrogen regulates female sexual behaviour
questions.solution: Androgens have anabolic effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism. Ovary is the primary female sex organ which produces one ovum during each menstrual cycle. Ovary produces two steriod hormones namely estrogen and progesterone. Ovary is composed of ovarian follicles and stromal tissues

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The estrogen is synthesised and secreted by the growing ovarian follicles
2. After ovulation, the ruptured follicle is converted to a structure called corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone
3. Progesterone supports pregnancy.
4. Progesterone acts on the mammary glands and stimulates the formation of alveoli (sac-like structures which store milk) and milk secretion.
questions.solution: The estrogen is synthesised and secreted by the growing ovarian follicles. After ovulation, the ruptured follicle is converted to a structure called corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Estrogen regulates female sexual behaviour
2. Progesterone helps in contraction during labour pain
3. Progesterone supports pregnancy
4. Females have only one ovary in the abdomen
5. Oxytocin also acts on the mammary glands and stimulates the formation of alveoli (sac-like structures which store milk) and milk secretion.
questions.solution: Estrogen regulates female sexual behaviour. Progesterone acts on the mammary glands and stimulates the formation of alveoli and milk secretion. Progesterone supports pregnancy. Females have a pair of ovaries located in the abdomen.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The atrial wall of heart secretes peptide hormone called atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), which decreases blood pressure
2. The juxtaglomerular cells of kidney produce a peptide hormone called erythropoietin which stimulates erythropoiesis
3. Endocrine cells present in different parts of the gastrointestinal tract secrete four major peptide hormones, namely gastrin, secretin, cholecystokinin and gastric inhibitory peptide
4. Hormones are also secreted by some tissues which are not endocrine glands.
questions.solution: The atrial wall of heart secretes peptide hormone called atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), which decreases blood pressure. The juxtaglomerular cells of kidney produce a peptide hormone called erythropoietin which stimulates erythropoiesis. Endocrine cells present in different parts of the gastrointestinal tract secrete four major peptide hormones, namely gastrin, secretin, cholecystokinin and gastric inhibitory peptide

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen
2. Secretin inhibits gastric secretion and motility
3. CCK acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively
4. GIP acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions
5. Hormones are also secreted by some tissues which are not endocrine glands.
questions.solution: Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen. GIP inhibits gastric secretion and motility. CCK acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively. Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The posterior pituitary is often considered not to be a true endocrine gland.
Reason (R): It synthesizes oxytocin and vasopressin under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) does not synthesize its own hormones; it only stores and releases hormones into the blood. Therefore, it is functionally an extension of the hypothalamus and is often not considered a true endocrine gland.

Reason (R) is incorrect because the posterior pituitary does not synthesize oxytocin and vasopressin. These hormones are actually synthesized by the hypothalamus and are transported axonally to the neurohypophysis, where they are stored and released.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Patients suffering from Diabetes mellitus and Diabetes insipidus both exhibit significant loss of water through urine.
Reason (R): Insulin is secreted by the $\beta$-cells of the pancreas, whereas ADH is synthesised by the hypothalamus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because both Diabetes mellitus and Diabetes insipidus are characterised by excessive urination leading to significant water loss and dehydration. In Diabetes mellitus, this is due to osmotic diuresis caused by glucose in the urine, while in Diabetes insipidus, it is due to the inability of the kidneys to conserve water.

Reason (R) is also factually correct as insulin is a peptide hormone secreted by the $\beta$-cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, and ADH (Anti-diuretic hormone) is synthesised by the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.

However, Reason (R) merely states the source of the hormones involved in these diseases and does not explain the physiological mechanism behind the shared symptom of water loss mentioned in Assertion (A). Therefore, both statements are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Zoology

Read the following statements regarding the hormones secreted by the endocrine cells present in different parts of the gastro-intestinal tract:

A. Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen.
B. Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates the secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.
C. Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts only on the gall bladder to stimulate the secretion of bile juice.
D. Gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP) stimulates gastric secretion and motility.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct: Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen.

Statement B is correct: Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates the secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.

Statement C is incorrect: Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts on both the pancreas and the gall bladder, stimulating the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice respectively. It does not act only on the gall bladder.

Statement D is incorrect: Gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP) inhibits gastric secretion and motility, rather than stimulating it.

Therefore, exactly two statements (A and B) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Adrenaline and noradrenaline cause an increase in the concentration of glucose in the blood.
Reason (R): Catecholamines stimulate glycogenesis and lipogenesis to provide rapid energy during emergency situations.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because adrenaline and noradrenaline (catecholamines) are hyperglycemic hormones that increase blood glucose levels to prepare the body for emergency situations.

Reason (R) is false because catecholamines stimulate the breakdown of glycogen (glycogenolysis), lipids (lipolysis), and proteins (proteolysis) to provide immediate energy. They do not stimulate the synthesis of glycogen (glycogenesis) or lipids (lipogenesis).

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Secretion of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) causes a decrease in blood pressure.
Reason (R): ANF is a peptide hormone that causes constriction of the blood vessels.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: The atrial wall of our heart secretes a peptide hormone called Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) in response to increased blood pressure, and its primary function is to decrease blood pressure.

Reason (R) is false: ANF decreases blood pressure by causing dilation (widening) of the blood vessels, not constriction. Vasoconstriction would increase blood pressure, which is the opposite of ANF's function.

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: When a person consumes a large amount of water, it significantly increases their body fluid volume. Which of the following correctly describes the subsequent physiological changes regarding the state of osmoreceptors, ADH release, and diuresis, respectively?
questions.solution:
An increase in body fluid volume due to excess water consumption switches off (suppresses) the osmoreceptors. This suppression halts the stimulation of the hypothalamus, leading to a decrease in the release of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) from the neurohypophysis. Without the action of ADH, water reabsorption in the latter parts of the renal tubules decreases, which results in enhanced diuresis (increased urine volume).

Option 1 is incorrect because fluid loss, not fluid gain, activates osmoreceptors.
Option 3 is incorrect because decreased ADH leads to enhanced, not prevented, diuresis.
Option 4 is incorrect because osmoreceptors are suppressed, not activated.

Answer: Suppressed, Decreased, Enhanced

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the physiological and cellular events occurring around the 14th day of a normal 28-day menstrual cycle:

(A) A rapid decline in estrogen secretion by the growing follicles triggers the LH surge.
(B) The primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division inside the tertiary follicle.
(C) The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone prior to ovulation.
(D) The Graafian follicle ruptures to release the secondary oocyte from the ovary.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is incorrect because a high concentration (peak) of estrogen exerts a positive feedback on the pituitary, triggering the LH surge, not a decline in estrogen.

Statement (B) is correct according to NCERT; the primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division within the tertiary follicle, which then matures into the Graafian follicle.

Statement (C) is incorrect because the corpus luteum is formed from the remnants of the Graafian follicle only after ovulation has occurred. Thus, it secretes progesterone during the luteal (post-ovulatory) phase, not prior to ovulation.

Statement (D) is correct as the LH surge induces the rupture of the Graafian follicle, releasing the secondary oocyte (ovulation).

Thus, exactly two statements ((B) and (D)) are correct.

Answer: Only two
